questions.clue: Rotate which subset is held out, refit on the rest, and average the held-out scores.

questions.clue: The chance a value is missing is independent of all observed and unobserved values.

questions.clue: Split the population into disjoint groups and draw a separate random sample from each group.

questions.clue: A second analyst gets the same tables using the original data and analysis code.

questions.clue: A regression drops each row that has any missing value among its fitted variables.

questions.clue: When a cross-validation fold contains exactly one observation, what prediction does that fold evaluate?

A prediction for a permanently reserved test set

questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 116, Cross-validation

questions.clue: When choosing between nested models with AIC, what can make the larger model preferable?
choices: The added term always forces the score down
The parameter count increases while maximized fit stays unchanged
The model reuses the same data without changing fit
The fit gain offsets the added parameter penalty
The reduced model has identical fit and fewer parameters

$k\ln(n)$

questions.clue: Copies of some patients are split across fit and evaluation sets. What is the clearest risk?

questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 207, Holdout estimate

questions.clue: In ridge regression, the penalty weight becomes very large. What happens to the penalized slopes?
choices: They approach their least squares values
questions.explanation: A very large squared-coefficient penalty strongly favors small slopes.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 370, Ridge regression

questions.clue: Why does a highly confident forecast get a large Brier loss when it predicts the wrong binary outcome?
choices: Its predicted event probability is near the observed indicator
Its predicted event probability is far from the observed indicator
The realized outcome is treated as unavailable
The score depends only on a classification threshold
The score rewards forecasting the rarer outcome
questions.answer: Its predicted event probability is far from the observed indicator
questions.explanation: Squared error penalizes probability forecasts most when they are far from the realized zero or one.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 64, Brier score

questions.concept: constant forecast baseline for brier score
questions.clue: For each held-out case, assign pᵢ = the event rate observed in training. What baseline is this when comparing Brier scores?

questions.clue: A classifier is evaluated on the same labeled records used to train it. What error was measured?
questions.explanation: Resubstitution evaluates the fitted rule on its own training observations.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 370, Resubstitution error rate

questions.clue: Why rerun cross-validation with freshly drawn folds when evaluating one fixed model specification?
choices: To remove the need for validation observations
To make each individual fit use the full dataset
To establish independence between all fold scores
To reduce dependence on a single random partition
To choose a causal interpretation without new assumptions
questions.answer: To reduce dependence on a single random partition
questions.explanation: Averaging over different partitions can make the estimate less sensitive to one random partition.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 116, Cross-validation

questions.clue: Two models describe the same pattern equally well. Which rule simply favors the model with fewer parameters?
questions.explanation: Parsimony prefers a simpler explanation when the competing descriptions fit equally well.

questions.concept: search scope of all subsets regression
questions.clue: What distinguishes all-subsets regression from forward selection?
choices: It begins with all variables and only deletes

It picks the best first predictor and only builds on that choice
It fits a single penalized model
It can compare models that are not on a single sequence of additions
questions.answer: It can compare models that are not on a single sequence of additions

questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 11, All subsets regression

questions.clue: A shop wants to validate a model for next month’s sales. Which holdout most closely mimics deployment?
choices: Evaluate all months used to fit the model
Hold out records with the largest fitted errors
Hold out only unusual sales days
Hold out the most recent month
Hold out the first month and train on later months

questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 207, Holdout estimate

questions.clue: Which penalty most directly encourages exact zeros among fitted slopes?
choices: λ times the sum of absolute slopes
λ times the sum of squared fitted values
λ times the sum of squared slopes
λ times the mean squared residual
λ times the squared residual sum

questions.clue: A random-number generator picks which survey module each person skips, independently of all responses. What mechanism is designed in?

choices: Missingness independent of the observed data

questions.clue: Which claim about MAR versus MNAR can the observed records alone generally support?
choices: They cannot settle whether missing values drive missingness
They distinguish both by sample size alone
They establish MAR whenever a balance check passes
They establish MCAR whenever missingness is below 5%
They establish MNAR whenever age predicts missingness
questions.answer: They cannot settle whether missing values drive missingness
questions.explanation: The dependence of missingness on unseen values cannot generally be determined from observations alone.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 279, Missing at random (MAR)

questions.clue: An analysis uses an outcome and a fixed set of predictors. Which missing values determine eligibility for a complete-case fit?
choices: Only missing values in unused fields
Missing values in any variable used in the fit
Missing outcomes only, regardless of predictor gaps
Only values absent in every sampled row
Only items marked missing by a second analyst
questions.answer: Missing values in any variable used in the fit
questions.explanation: Complete cases have all the variables required for the particular analysis.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 94, Complete case analysis

questions.clue: Under available-case analysis, which records can inform the covariance of X and Y when a separate variable Z is also in the dataset?
choices: Records with either X or Y observed, regardless of Z
Only records containing X, Y and Z
All records, including those with neither X nor Y
Records with both X and Y observed, regardless of Z
Records with Z and either X or Y
questions.answer: Records with both X and Y observed, regardless of Z
questions.explanation: Each covariance uses observed measurements of both variables in that pair.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 27, Available case analysis

questions.clue: If every missing value is replaced by the observed mean, what property of the variable is preserved exactly?
questions.explanation: Values added at the original mean do not change the completed mean.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 213, Imputation

questions.clue: At the last visit, likely missing responses would have kept rising. What direction of error does carrying the earlier value forward tend to introduce for those cases?
choices: Attenuation toward the final mean of completers
Symmetric errors around the unseen value
No change in the estimated final mean
questions.explanation: Replacing a later rising response with its earlier, lower value tends to underestimate it.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 242, Last observation carried forward

questions.clue: Which property is guaranteed when every missing blood type is filled by a donor from the current survey?

Imputed blood type counts match the population counts
The estimated sampling variance is unchanged
Blood type becomes independent of other variables
Each imputation is a blood type already recorded in the survey
questions.answer: Each imputation is a blood type already recorded in the survey
questions.explanation: A hot-deck donor supplies an actually recorded category from the current survey.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 208, Hot deck

questions.clue: A fully recorded test score predicts both completion and the missing outcome. Which imputation choice uses this information?
choices: Impute the overall observed outcome mean
Drop the score and use case deletion
Include the test score as a predictor
Choose donors without using the score
Use the missingness rate as the only predictor
questions.answer: Include the test score as a predictor
questions.explanation: The auxiliary score helps predict the outcome and account for differences in who has it recorded.

In Rubin’s pooling rules, what does this factor multiply?

questions.clue: Why should an analyst avoid deriving a standard error from only one completed dataset after multiple imputation?

It ignores uncertainty across the completed datasets
It uses the original number of incomplete records
It forces the confidence interval to be centered at zero

questions.clue: New hires miss the questionnaire more often and have higher satisfaction. What can happen to a mean calculated only from complete cases?

It is unchanged by the missingness pattern

questions.clue: In exact EM, an iteration starts at parameters with finite observed-data likelihood. Which change across the iteration is guaranteed?

The completed-data likelihood increases for every completion

questions.clue: Filling each blank with one fitted value and treating that dataset as complete omits which uncertainty?

Measurement error in the recorded units of the outcome
Rounding error in the listed sample size
The distance between observed and fitted means

questions.clue: To estimate a population total using a sample ratio of workers to kiosks, what auxiliary quantity anchors the extrapolation?

The number of workers at the largest sampled kiosk
The share of sampled kiosks with any workers
The known number of kiosks in the population

questions.clue: When combining poststratum means to match the target population, which weights should be used?

Target population shares for the poststrata
The inverse of each group’s observed mean

The frame mean cannot vary across survey years
Every possible draw includes the same frame units
The target population always equals the frame

$\sqrt{1-\frac{n}{N}}$

Use the chances directly as weights
Base weight only on each firm’s reported outcome

questions.clue: An analysis reads from a path beginning with the author’s personal home folder. Which edit makes the inputs easier to locate elsewhere?

Use a path relative to the project root

questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: Cleaning, fitting, and plotting scripts are all provided. What should one top-level command do first?
questions.explanation: Fitting requires cleaned inputs, and plotting requires the fitted results.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: An article’s link points to a software branch whose contents keep changing. What identifier fixes the version used in the article?
choices: The filename of the analysis script
questions.explanation: A commit identifier selects a particular revision even after the branch advances.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Version control. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#version-control

questions.clue: Two teams report different outlier exclusions on the same raw file. What comparison can diagnose the source?
choices: Compare the mean of a variable uninvolved in exclusion
Compare the final sample sizes only
Compare the filenames of the cleaned files
Compare the plot captions for the final report
Compare the exact exclusion rules and their retained row IDs
questions.answer: Compare the exact exclusion rules and their retained row IDs
questions.explanation: The recorded rules and row sets reveal which exclusions differed despite a shared input.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: A download endpoint always serves the most recent file. Which workflow prevents a rerun from silently using revised data?
choices: Keep the request URL while clearing local archives
Sort the latest file in the original row order
Download the latest file and log its size
Use the endpoint again and check its column names
Read an archived copy and verify its checksum
questions.answer: Read an archived copy and verify its checksum
questions.explanation: An archived copy supplies the original version, and the checksum checks for changes to its bytes.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue: Confidential survey records cannot be released. What most helps authorized researchers reproduce the analysis?
choices: Replace the data with unrelated examples and omit that change
Provide the workflow and document the secure data-access route
Publish model code without identifying its intended inputs
questions.answer: Provide the workflow and document the secure data-access route
questions.explanation: An approved route to the original records, along with the workflow, lets qualified readers rerun the study.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Lab 4, Reproducibility. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/labs/lab4-reproducibility.html

questions.clue: A rerun completes without errors. Which artifact helps determine whether it recovered the reported numbers?
choices: A list of commands that ran
A versioned set of expected numeric results
A count of figures in the folder
questions.answer: A versioned set of expected numeric results
questions.explanation: The numerical output must be compared with the published or archived values.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Lab 4, Reproducibility. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/labs/lab4-reproducibility.html

questions.clue: A published figure was cropped in an image editor after the plot script ran. Which change most directly makes the published figure reproducible?
choices: Save another copy of the raw inputs
Document only the plot package version
Rename the script with the publication date
Add the cropping step to the workflow
Rerun the analysis after changing its seed
questions.answer: Add the cropping step to the workflow
questions.explanation: An explicit cropping step lets the analysis regenerate the final figure as shown.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: An agency changes its open data daily. Which acquisition detail identifies when a snapshot was obtained?
choices: The date and time of retrieval
questions.answer: The date and time of retrieval
questions.explanation: The retrieval time links the snapshot to the state of a changing source.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue: A published regression includes only one of four tested adjustment sets. Which record makes the published result rerunnable?
choices: The exact adjustment set used by the report
The order in which the figures are numbered
A version of the raw data alone
The names of the four sets without their terms
The total number of candidate covariates
questions.answer: The exact adjustment set used by the report
questions.explanation: The reported model specification tells readers which predictors to include when rebuilding the fit.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: An analysis sets one seed at startup. Adding a random draw before it splits the data changes the split. What explains this?
choices: The seed selects a fresh random sequence for each command
The output depends only on the rounded estimates
The dataset content must have changed
The added draw advances the random-number generator state
The added draw changes the sample size
questions.answer: The added draw advances the random-number generator state
questions.explanation: With the same seed, later values depend on how many earlier random draws consumed the sequence.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue: A raw-data cleaning step takes a day. Which practice permits fast reruns while retaining the ability to verify the cleaning?
choices: Keep the cleaned artifact and delete the raw input
Store the cleaned artifact and retain the cleaning script and raw input
Overwrite the cleaning script with a copy of the fitted model
Keep the raw input and rewrite cleaning manually each time
Store the final figures and discard the cleaned artifact
questions.answer: Store the cleaned artifact and retain the cleaning script and raw input
questions.explanation: An intermediate file speeds reuse, while the original input and script permit full regeneration.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: The same script generates every bootstrap table by reading settings from a command line. Which item should accompany the published table?
choices: The exact argument values used for that table
The code documentation without the selected settings
A list of possible argument names only
The names of the output files from all runs
The date when the script was first written
questions.answer: The exact argument values used for that table
questions.explanation: The values passed to the script determine the analysis actually performed.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: The analysis requires specific Python and system-library versions. Which shared artifact can describe both layers together?
choices: A compressed copy of the input data
A list of Python import statements
questions.explanation: A container recipe can specify system libraries and Python dependencies together.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: An author says a recent edit changed the model formula. Which record directly shows the lines changed between two saved revisions?
questions.explanation: A diff displays the specific insertions and deletions between the two revisions.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, Version control. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#version-control

questions.clue: Two complete reruns differ. The input snapshot matches, but software versions and commands differ. What first comparison isolates the software’s role?
choices: Change both the commands and the environment
Take an average of the two reported estimates
Hold the commands fixed and vary only the environment
Change the rounding rule and rerun only the plots
Replace the inputs and keep the other differences
questions.answer: Hold the commands fixed and vary only the environment
questions.explanation: Varying only the environment isolates it as the candidate source of a difference.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Lab 4, Reproducibility. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/labs/lab4-reproducibility.html

questions.clue: Which check is best at finding a hidden dependence on old files produced by an earlier run?
choices: Open only the figures in another viewer
Run the documented workflow from an empty output folder
Read the final table twice without rerunning
Compare the existing files by modification date
Copy all the old output files into a renamed folder
questions.answer: Run the documented workflow from an empty output folder
questions.explanation: An empty output folder forces the workflow to recreate each output it relies on.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Lab 4, Reproducibility. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/labs/lab4-reproducibility.html
